subject: QBR hiring prioritization & req deconfliction
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenwood Talent <talent@greenwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR hiring prioritization & req deconfliction

Team —

As we prep for the QBR next week I want to lock decisions on the open reqs that materially affect our cost / delivery forecast. Attached are two artifacts: a heatmap of open reqs by org impact and a QBR headcount impact workbook with baseline vs prioritized scenarios. TL;DR: we cannot approve all open reqs without pushing our cost target above the Q4 plan.

Asks:
- Please review the attached heatmap and flag any reqs you believe are "non-negotiable" for delivery (reply with req id).
- For roles in your teams that are mid-cycle (offer stage or vendor pipeline), mark them as either: Hire / Hold / Backfill-only.
- If you want a swap (approve one req only if another is deprioritized), propose the explicit swap in your reply.

I propose the following guardrails for decisions:
- Prioritize revenue-impacting and security/compliance hires.
- Defer lower-priority IC growth hires and stretch to contractors for Q4 where feasible.
- Any req not explicitly approved by EOD Monday will be auto-placed into a temporary freeze for the QBR window.

Greenwood — thanks for the pipeline snapshot; please keep the candidate lists for the two priority Eng reqs open but pause outreach for the rest pending our call.

I'll collate replies and publish a single decision memo Monday morning.

Markus Klein
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: QBR_headcount_impact_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB), open-req-heatmap.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR hiring prioritization & req deconfliction

Markus — thanks for the artifacts. Quick notes from Talent ops: 

- I reviewed offers in flight: two senior TPM offers (REQ-2419, REQ-2421) are verbal-accept and scheduled for signed paperwork this week. Recommend marking those as Hire — moving them to Hold will risk losing both.
- Internship program (REQ-INT-2026) has low org impact for Q4. Recommend Hold/Freeze and re-evaluate in Jan.
- Contractor runway: we have budget for extending three contractor engagements for 10 weeks (engineering infra, SRE, and data labeling). That covers immediate backfill needs w/o new headcount.

Proposed explicit swaps: 
- Approve one mid-senior SWE hire for Platform (REQ-2388) only if we freeze a non-customer-facing IC growth req in Growth (REQ-2395).

I'll mark the pipeline statuses in the shared workbook and update candidate notes so Greenwood has visibility.

Laura Bennett
Head of Talent & People Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR hiring prioritization & req deconfliction

Agree with Laura on the TPMs — please treat those as Hires. From Eng across the board: 

- Critical: REQ-2388 (Platform mid-senior SWE) — blocking a planned rollout for new batch-serve infra if not staffed. This is a revenue-timing risk; mark as Hire unless we take a temporary workaround that will cost ~2-3% throughput.
- Medium: REQ-2403 (ML infra engineer) — can be deferred to Jan if we accept a slower model onboarding cadence.
- Low: REQ-2395 (Growth IC) — scope can be absorbed by current team for Q4 with minor roadmap slip.

If the committee is open to a single swap: Approve REQ-2388 (Platform SWE) and freeze REQ-2395 (Growth) — that aligns with the revenue-impact rule.

Also added a short note in the workbook under the Platform tab with the proposed mitigation (fallback rollout plan) in case we cannot fill 2388 immediately.

Jonas Weber
Director, Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR hiring prioritization & req deconfliction

Thanks — pulling this together into the decision memo now. Final decisions based on the replies: 

- Approve (Hire): REQ-2419 (Senior TPM), REQ-2421 (Senior TPM), REQ-2388 (Platform mid-senior SWE).
- Approve as Contractor/backfill (No new headcount): REQ-2409 (SRE backfill), REQ-2416 (labeling ops).
- Freeze / Hold: REQ-INT-2026 (Internship), REQ-2395 (Growth IC), REQ-2403 (ML infra engineer) — defer to Jan evaluation window.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Laura: finalize paperwork for REQ-2419 & REQ-2421 (Offers out & signed by 11/24).
- Jonas: short mitigation doc for REQ-2388 fallback (deliverable: rollout plan + throughput impact) by 11/24.
- TA / Greenwood: pause outreach for non-approved reqs; continue active process for Platform and TPM candidates.
- Ops: update QBR headcount workbook with final statuses (I've attached v3; please confirm changes in the Drive link).

I'll circulate the formal memo and include these items in the QBR slide set. If anyone has an urgent objection, flag before EOD Monday or the freeze stands.

Markus Klein
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
